## The application notice

This is the standard AGPL-3.0 notice, filled in for this project. It belongs at the top of
source files and in the README:

```
{{PRODUCT_NAME}} — brand identity and business document tooling
Copyright (C) {{YEAR}} {{LEGAL_ENTITY}}

This program is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
it under the terms of the GNU Affero General Public License as published

but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the
GNU Affero General Public License for more details.

You should have received a copy of the GNU Affero General Public License
along with this program.  If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
```

Note **"or (at your option) any later version"** — that phrasing is what lets the project move
to a future AGPL revision without tracking down every contributor. Dropping it would quietly
give that up.

## Why AGPL rather than GPL

**Section 13.** If you run a modified version of this program and let other people interact with
it over a network, you must offer those users the source of your modified version. Plain GPL
does not reach network use, which for a tool that is primarily used in a browser would mean the
copyleft covers almost nothing.

That obligation binds us exactly as it binds everyone else. `TERMS.md` §8 states where the
source of our own running instance can be obtained, because a company that chose the AGPL and
then quietly ignored §13 would deserve every bit of the reaction it got.

## What the licence does not cover

**Trademarks are not licensed by the AGPL** — see `TRADEMARK.md`. **The hosted service is not
governed by the AGPL** — see `TERMS.md`. Those are separate instruments on purpose; conflating
them is the usual mistake.
